response.query: Which open-science practices (pre-registration, shared code/data, documented pipelines) and governance models best balance methodological transparency and student privacy when publishing methods and datasets?
response.answer: Pre-registration, shared code/data with privacy protections, and documented pipelines best balance transparency and student privacy in open science. Anonymization and data access agreements are key governance models.

results.title: Open Science - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: Open Science is defined as an umbrella term that encompasses the idea that scientific knowledge should be openly accessible, transparent, rigorous, reproducible, and inclusive, reflecting fundamental features of the scientific endeavor. Open science practices can refer to various aspects of research, including data, methods, materials, and analysis code. Open science practices are based on principles of transparency and wide sharing of information, and these practices are increasingly common in studies of psychophysiology (Clayson et al., 2021b; Clayson et al., 2022c). Many of the studies cited in this review embraced open science practices, and their data processing or statistical analysis code is openly available. Open research is both a philosophical approach (Fecher & Friesike, 2014) and a set of practices; the latter of which include, but are not limited to, the preregistration of study protocols, as well as the sharing of study materials, data, and outputs (see for example Kramer & Jeroen, 2018).
